Subject: Mutual plan: performance snapshot + close timeline for Nimbus POC

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our MAP, we want to lock the benchmarking window and finalize which model variants we should include in the POC evaluation. Attached I’ve dropped a working MAP (nimbus_map_v3.xlsx) and a short checklist for the bench run. Key asks from our side to keep the close timeline intact (targeting contract signature by 2026-07-15):

- Confirm the primary SLA target: 99th pct latency < 300ms for single-turn lookups, TTFT < 150ms for streaming-first token.
- Confirm peak concurrency target: 250 concurrent sessions (simulated conversational flows).
- Confirm quality metric: top-1 factual accuracy on your FAQ/regulatory QA set (we’ll run a 1k sample) + manual review of 50 fallbacks.

To make the MAP actionable we propose running the following model variants from our catalog during the bench window (2 business days):
- rw-7B-q4 (low-cost quantized) — baseline for cost-latency tradeoff
- rw-13B-fp16 (medium) — expected best quality/latency balance
- rw-65B-8bit (high-quality) — best accuracy, higher cost/TTFT

I’ve tentatively scheduled bench runs 2026-06-28 -> 2026-06-29. Can you confirm availability for the engineering window and whether Nimbus can provide a fixed prompt/eval set by EOD 2026-06-26?

Thanks —
Karthik

Karthik —

All good, thanks. We can commit to the 6/28-6/29 window for the bench. Ben will hand over the 1k eval set (mix of short FAQ queries, longer regulatory prompts, and multi-turn symptom triage flows) by end of day Friday (6/26). A couple of constraints from our side:

- Any model variant that exhibits TTFT > 350ms under 50 concurrent simulated agents is a non-starter for the patient-facing flow.
- We need token-level cost projections per 10k queries for each variant — our finance team will use that for the internal procurement MA.

Also, for the production roll we prefer a staged canary with auto-fallback (higher-latency model) rather than a blunt switch. Please include fallback latency behavior in your report.

—Anna

Subject: Bench run: kickoff & test harness details

Morning —

We’re live for the benchmark today. Quick notes on the harness and what we’ll capture (so the MAP timeline stays accurate):

- Workload: 1k eval set (Anna/Ben) + synthetic concurrency stress tests at increments: 10, 50, 100, 250 concurrent simulated sessions.
- Metrics captured: TTFT (ms), median token latency (ms/token), throughput (tokens/sec), 95/99th pct latency, error rate (timeouts/502s), and cost-per-10k-queries estimate (USD).
- Routing policy: single-region (us-west) with burst capacity enabled. We’ll also exercise an auto-fallback policy — route to rw-13B-fp16 if rw-65B-8bit is unavailable, and to rw-7B-q4 as last resort.

I’ll push raw logs (benchmark_logs.tar.gz) and a summary PDF to Drive when complete. Expected first pass summary by EOD 6/29.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Lowe <anna.lowe@NimbusHealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-29T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Benchmark summary (first pass) — recommended variant & next steps

Anna/Ben —

Summary of the first-pass results (full PDF attached: nimbus_bench_summary.pdf). Key numbers below are median/95th/99th where shown. Cost numbers are Redwood estimate including tokenized prompt + response for the eval set. All runs executed in us-west with the MAP routing policy.

1) rw-7B-q4 (quantized) — baseline
- TTFT: 82 ms median / 140 ms 95th / 190 ms 99th
- Median per-token latency: 6.4 ms/token
- Throughput: ~480 tokens/sec (single replica)
- Concurrency behavior: stable to 100 concurrent sessions; significant tail growth at 250 (99th ~520 ms)
- Quality: top-1 factual accuracy on eval set = 86%
- Cost estimate (per 10k queries): $62

2) rw-13B-fp16 (mid) — balanced
- TTFT: 118 ms median / 210 ms 95th / 290 ms 99th
- Median per-token latency: 9.8 ms/token
- Throughput: ~320 tokens/sec (single replica)
- Concurrency behavior: handles 250 concurrent sessions with 99th ~310 ms when autoscaled to 2 replicas
- Quality: top-1 factual accuracy = 92%
- Cost estimate (per 10k queries): $185

3) rw-65B-8bit (high quality) — premium
- TTFT: 240 ms median / 360 ms 95th / 520 ms 99th
- Median per-token latency: 18.2 ms/token
- Throughput: ~120 tokens/sec (single replica)
- Concurrency behavior: needs 4 replicas to meet 250 concurrent sessions target; autoscaling introduces warm-up TTFT spikes
- Quality: top-1 factual accuracy = 96% (best on regulatory prompts)
- Cost estimate (per 10k queries): $720

Observed behaviors and tradeoffs:
- rw-7B-q4 meets strict TTFT targets at low concurrency but fails Nimbus’ 250-concurrency requirement at acceptable tail latency.
- rw-13B-fp16 provides the best balance — meets TTFT and concurrency when configured with 2 dedicated replicas and the MAP canary rollout with rw-65B fallback for the highest-quality queries.
- rw-65B-8bit is highest quality but cost and TTFT make it unsuitable as primary for patient-facing flows; best used as fallback for high-criticality or regulatory responses.

Recommendation (aligned with MAP & procurement timeline):
- Production POC config: primary = rw-13B-fp16 (2 replicas dedicated), fallback = rw-65B-8bit for flagged regulatory queries, last-resort fallback = rw-7B-q4 for capacity surge.
- Close timeline: propose final SOW and pricing by 2026-07-08, signature target 2026-07-15. Finance asks: include the per-10k cost lines above and a 12-month committed discount scenario.

Next steps:
- Vanessa will prepare a concise pricing worksheet for procurement. (Vanessa: can you add committed-commit bands and updated unit economics?)
- Marissa will own SLA wording for the SOW and fallback availability guarantees.
- Anna/Ben: please confirm whether you want rw-65B fallback enabled in canary or only post-cutover.

Thanks — quick sync tomorrow if useful.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Benchmark summary (first pass) — recommended variant & next steps

Thanks for the rapid turnaround — this is helpful. Quick responses:

- We agree with the recommended config: rw-13B-fp16 primary + rw-65B-8bit fallback for regulatory. Please enable fallback only for flagged queries during canary.
- Finance requested a committed-12mo quote (bands: 0-250k, 250k-1M, 1M+) and a short note on how autoscaling would affect committed usage accounting. Vanessa — we’ll need that to move procurement.
- One operational ask: can you add a short run showing fallback latency (rw-13B -> rw-65B) under a simulated failover? That will help our SREs sign off.

If you can get the pricing worksheet and the failover bench by 7/02 we’ll proceed to draft PO language. Targeting signature 7/15 per MAP.

—Anna
